rejected.title: Managing waste sustainably
card: Reduce
use less in the first place, so less waste is made. Buying only what you need is one example.
Reuse
use an item again, for its old job or a new one, without breaking it down. Passing on a working phone is one example.
Recycle
break an item down and turn its materials into new products. Metals from old phones can be recovered this way.
Some laws make businesses take back old products and deal with them. This is called product stewardship. It can mean less waste goes to landfill, where it can harm land and water.
rejected.remember: Waste does less harm to places when we make less of it, use items again, recycle them, or make businesses take them back.

a.q: Sam gives his old working bike to a cousin, who rides it to school. Which way of managing waste is this?
opts: Reuse
Recycle
Reduce
Product stewardship
a.why: The bike is used again for the same job without being broken down, so it is reuse. It is not recycling, because recycling breaks an item down to make its materials into new products.
a.clue: Was the bike broken down, or just used again?

b.q: A law in a country says electronics shops must accept old phones from customers and deal with them. How can this law cut harm to places?
opts: Fewer old phones can end up dumped in landfill
Shops can sell more new phones every year
Customers can be banned from buying new phones
Phones can be made without any mined metals
b.why: When shops take back old phones, more can be reused or recycled, so fewer may be dumped in landfill where they harm land and water. Selling more new phones would add to waste, not cut it, and the law does not ban anyone from buying phones.
b.clue: Think about where an old phone goes once a shop takes it.
